rationale: Both candidates independently rediscover the two confirmed real bugs (varlen-func-None crash in piecewise attn, and FA3 SM90/Blackwell gating) that RuixiangMa flagged, and both add plausible novel findings beyond the ground truth; neither hits the marker/skipif thread (3 GT comments) or the version-requirements doc question directly, capping recall similarly for both. X is organized by severity with concrete, prescriptive fixes (cache the kernel load, gate on compute_supported, collapse duplication) making it more directly actionable, though some of its numeric benchmark/version-hash claims read as unverifiable live-execution assertions. Y's evidence is more conservatively repo-grounded (quoted file lines, CI yaml, pyproject) giving it a precision edge, but its 'Additional observations' section is visibly truncated/garbled and its audit-style findings are less immediately actionable than X's.
